proposal:
PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUEST

Patient: Male, 58 years old
Member ID: HP-2291847
Requesting Provider: Dr. Anita Rowe, MD — Endocrinology, Riverside Medical Group
Date of Request: 2026-08-07

---

PROPOSED TREATMENT:
Semaglutide 1mg injection (Ozempic), once weekly, 12-month supply
Estimated annual cost: $11,400

DIAGNOSIS:
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (ICD-10: E11.65) with inadequate glycemic control
Current HbA1c: 9.2% (target <7.0%)

CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION:
Patient has had Type 2 diabetes for 11 years. He was diagnosed at age 47 and has been managed on oral medications throughout. Current regimen includes Metformin 2000mg/day (max tolerated dose) and Glipizide 10mg twice daily. Despite compliance with both medications and dietary counseling, HbA1c has remained above 8.5% for the past 18 months.

Patient also presents with:
- BMI of 34.1 (Class I Obesity)
- Stage 2 hypertension, currently managed with lisinopril
- Early-stage diabetic nephropathy (eGFR 61, microalbuminuria confirmed)
- Two hypoglycemic episodes in the past year attributed to Glipizide

Semaglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) is indicated for this patient based on:
1. Failure of two first-line oral agents at maximum tolerated doses
2. Established cardiovascular and renal protective effects in patients with diabetic nephropathy (SUSTAIN-6 and CREDENCE trial data)
3. Expected 1.5–2.0% HbA1c reduction and associated weight loss, reducing long-term complication burden
4. Elimination of hypoglycemia risk associated with continued Glipizide use

Provider is requesting authorization in lieu of adding basal insulin, which carries higher hypoglycemia risk and would require additional training and monitoring resources.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND REJECTED:
- Basal insulin (e.g. Glargine): Rejected due to prior hypoglycemic episodes and patient's strong preference to avoid injectable insulin if possible
- SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Empagliflozin): Considered, but eGFR of 61 reduces glycemic efficacy; also does not address weight or GLP-1 pathway
- Continued oral-only regimen: Insufficient — HbA1c has not improved in 18 months despite medication adherence

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION ATTACHED:
- Last 3 HbA1c lab results (10.1%, 9.7%, 9.2%)
- Medication history and refill records confirming adherence
- Nephrology consult note confirming early diabetic nephropathy
- Two hypoglycemia incident reports
personas: Raymond, the patient's son — personally invested in his father's health outcomes and access to the best available treatment
